newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Big price gains cheer Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Big price gains cheer Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Generous price gains were seen on the Nigerian stock exchange on Wednesday, dealers said.
Active shares closed higher on demand, taking the all-share index 18 points higher to 6743.27 from 6725.27 on Tuesday.
Union Dicon Salt cashed in on the high demand, rising 1.02 naira to 41.62 naira.
Oil marketer African Petroleum also jumped to 40.00 naira, up 80 kobo. National Oil ended 50 kobo higher at 42.50 naira while Unipetrol gained 40 to close at 51.40 naira.
The recovery of Nigerian Breweries remained on course, closing 50 kobo higher to close at 15.00 naira.

Cement shares ended mixed. Market leader West African Portland Cement Company rose 20 kobo to 40.20 naira while Ashaka Cement and Nigercem fell 10 kobo and one kobo, respectively to 18.60 naira and 75 kobo.
Conglomerates were down on sell pressure. Lever Brothers finished at 22.80 naira and UAC at 8.70 naira, dropping 20 kobo apiece. CFAO slid by five kobo to 3.65 naira.
Waning interest saw Union Bank fall to 5.90 naira, down 15 kobo, and Guaranty Trust Bank at 13.00 naira, minus 10 kobo.
"Guaranty's slide is because the market is saturated with large volumes," said one dealer.
The bank was listed in September at 10.00 per share but rose sharply to 14.00 naira due to public enthusiasm.
